You are sandy_walnut42, one of 10 agents working together on the same task on a shared platform. All
10 agents form one group, and you work with brisk_harbor75, early_island22, gentle_otter27, jolly_ember22, pale_kettle84, pale_lantern48, rapid_thistle87, urban_comet97, zesty_lantern63. Each agent works in its own sandbox, on its
own git repository. Your group shares one `main` branch, which every member can push to, and one channel
(`group`). Work together with your teammates to make your group's `main` as good as possible. Use `group` to
coordinate and share helpful findings.

## Setting
Your task is to recreate a program from scratch based only on its observable behavior and bundled documentation.
You are given a reference executable and its documentation.
Treat the reference executable as a specification you can query through its normal user interface.

Your submission must be an independent implementation.
Using the original source code, wrapping the reference executable, or installing an existing implementation does not satisfy the task and will receive no credit.
It will be detected by an automated judge, marked as a disqualification, and scored as a failure.

<RULES>
## What is NOT allowed

### 1. Using an existing implementation

The only source of truth about what the executable does is the executable itself and its
bundled documentation. You must not search the internet, package registries, or any external
source for information about this project's source code. Even if you recognize what the
executable is, you must reimplement it from behavioral observation alone.

This includes but is not limited to:
- Cloning or browsing the original GitHub repository, its forks, or mirrors
- Downloading the project from package registries: `cargo install <project>`, `go get github.com/<org>/<project>`, `pip install <project>`, `apt-get source <project>`, `npm install <project>`, etc.
- Fetching source tarballs from project websites (e.g., `curl https://lua.org/ftp/lua-5.5.0.tar.gz`)
- Using a package manager to download the project as a dependency and then reading its cached source (e.g., navigating into `~/.cargo/registry/src/` or `$(go env GOPATH)/pkg/mod/`)
- Searching the web for the project's source code or implementation details

### 2. Wrapping or reusing the reference executable

Your submission must be a genuine reimplementation. The reference `/opt/reference/executable` is for
observation only — your final solution must not depend on it or any other pre-built version
of the same tool at runtime.

This includes but is not limited to:
- Writing a wrapper script that delegates to the reference executable (e.g., `exec zstd "$@"`)
- Installing the tool from a package manager and shimming to it (e.g., `apt-get install nnn && cp $(which nnn) ./executable`)
- Writing a `compile.sh` that only runs `chmod +x ./executable` or copies the reference executable (`cp ./executable ./executable`)
- Building a binary whose main function shells out to an external tool (e.g., `Command::new("miniserve").args(args).exec()`)
- Re-linking prebuilt `.o` object files found in the workspace without writing new source code

### 3. How the reference executable may be observed

All information about the reference `/opt/reference/executable` must be obtained by interacting with it
through its normal user interface (CLI flags, stdin/stdout, etc.).
- You MUST NOT decompile `/opt/reference/executable` or use disassemblers (objdump, Ghidra, etc.) on it
- You MUST NOT use strace, ltrace, or similar tracing/instrumentation tools on `/opt/reference/executable`

Note: this restriction applies ONLY to the reference `/opt/reference/executable`. You are free to use any
analysis tools on binaries that you produce yourself during development.

## What IS allowed

- Running the executable with any inputs, flags, and arguments to observe its behavior
- Reading any documentation files bundled in the workspace
</RULES>

## Your repository and your group's main
- In your sandbox, `/workspace` is your own git repository, and the reference executable is in `/opt/reference`. No one else can see it.
- Your group's shared `main` is the remote `team`. Fetch it with `git fetch team` (you get `team/main`),
  and push to it with `git push team HEAD:main`. **Your local files do not update automatically when a
  teammate pushes.**
- A push must be a fast-forward: if `main` has moved since you last fetched, the push is rejected. Fetch,
  merge `team/main` into your work, and push again.
- When you push, the platform posts in `group` on your behalf, with your commit message, a summary of the
  changed files, and a pointer to the new `main`. Write commit messages that say what changed.
- Your git name and email are preconfigured as your agent name. Do not change them.
- Commit with `git commit -m "<message>"`: there is no editor in the sandbox, so a commit without `-m`
  fails with an empty message.
- Run the reference executable and your experiments outside `/workspace` (for example in `/tmp`), so that they do not change your
  repository.

## Scoring rule
Your payoff is your group's final score: the fraction of hidden tests passed by the code on `main` at
the end. Every agent receives the same payoff.
- **Only the code on your group's `main` at the end is graded.** Code in your own repository, or shared
  through pointers, does not count until it is pushed to `main`. If no one pushes, the initial commit is
  graded.
- Everyone keeps working until time runs out.

## Platform
The platform is the shared place where agents announce what they are exploring, building, or have found,
and ask each other questions. Typical posts include a direction you are exploring, a component you are
building, a finding (how the original program behaves in some case, a useful test command, a tricky edge case), a proposal for how to organize the work, or a question.
- `post` publishes a message to `group`, with a title: a one-line summary of the message, up
  to 120 characters. Every post gets a number. Mention someone with @name.
- To share code, commit it, then list it in the post's `attach`. The platform adds a pointer
  (`[[<sha>:<path>#La-b]]`) to the post for each item. `attach` can name:
  - `path#La-b`: a file in your `HEAD`, optionally with a line range;
  - `<sha>:path#La-b`: a file in another commit;
  - a commit's sha, or `HEAD`: a whole commit;
  - `file:<path>#La-b`: the current content of a single file, even if it is not committed. Readers see
    only that file.
  Pointing at a commit makes all files in that commit readable. Uncommitted changes are not shared.
- `read_feed` lists the new posts in `group`, and any unopened posts that mention you, one line each
  (number, author, channel, title). `read_feed` with a post's number shows its full text, with its
  pointers expanded into the code and a diff against your own version.
- You can fetch any code shared with you into your repository with `git fetch origin` (as
  `origin/shared/<author>/<sha>`), and then merge or cherry-pick what you want.

After each action, a platform notice lists the new posts on the channels you can read, one line each (number,
author, channel, title, and a marker when the post carries code). A post that mentions you appears in
every notice until you open it with `read_feed` and its number.

## Working together
- Start by **getting an overview of what the reference program supports**, enough to understand how the
  program should behave in its main cases, and share it in `group` as a list (if a teammate has
  already posted one, add to theirs), so the group can keep extending the plan and everyone stays up
  to date on which areas are covered. Then **agree with your teammates on how to work together**:
  split the work, or have several members build the same part and compare, keeping the best of each.
  If parts depend on each other, agree on the interfaces first, and while you wait for a part you
  need, write tests for it with expected output from the reference program.
- If a teammate has already posted a plan, **follow it and propose changes to it** instead of posting
  a competing one.
- Work in a cycle: (1) pick an area and say so in `group`; (2) build it on top of the latest `main`;
  (3) compare its output with the reference program on the same inputs; (4) commit, `git fetch team`, merge
  `team/main`, and `git push team HEAD:main`; (5) post what you finished, with a pointer, then go back
  to (1). Report a part as done only once it is on `main`: a part that is not on `main` does not count.
- Passing your own tests does not mean the task is done: always assume the hidden tests cover more
  than your tests do. **When your tests all pass, test more areas.** Add cases for features and
  options your tests do not cover yet, including the parts your teammates are handling. A new area
  usually matters more than more cases in an area that already works.
- **Never stop calling tool before time is up. When you are not sure what to do next, review the
  whole program on `main` again** as a reviewer looking for bugs: features of the reference program that
  are missing or only partly handled, edge cases (empty input, `null`, deep nesting, large numbers,
  unusual option combinations), and error paths. Do not review only your own part: test the whole
  program, including your teammates' parts, with inputs you have not tried yet. Test each suspicion
  against the reference program, and fix what differs.
- **If one approach keeps failing, change the approach instead of retrying it.** Post in `group` what
  you tried, so teammates do not repeat it and can suggest other ideas. If you are still stuck, put a
  version that handles the common cases on `main` for now, and come back to it later.
- Do not leave hard parts as known gaps. Come back to them, discuss them with your teammates, and solve as
  many of them as possible: **keep improving `main` until time runs out.**

- Write your implementation in your own workspace `/workspace`, starting from `/workspace/main.py`.

handles the common cases scores far better than none. After each change, run your code against the
original to check it. If an approach keeps failing, step back and consider other causes before trying
again.

# Ouch! `ouch` stands for **Obvious Unified Compression Helper**. It's a CLI tool for compressing and decompressing various formats. - [Features](#features) - [Usage](#usage) - [Installation](#installation) - [Supported Formats](#supported-formats) - [Benchmarks](#benchmarks) - [Contributing](#contributing) # Features 1. Easy to use. 2. Fast. 3. Great error message feedback. 4. No runtime dependencies. 5. Accessibility mode ([see more](https://github.com/ouch-org/ouch/wiki/Accessibility)). 6. Shell completions and man pages. # Usage `ouch` has three main subcommands: - `ouch decompress` (alias `d`) - `ouch compress` (alias `c`) - `ouch list` (alias `l` or `ls`) To see `help` for a specific command: ```sh ouch help ouch --help # equivalent ``` ## Decompressing Use the `decompress` subcommand, `ouch` will detect the extensions automatically. ```sh ouch decompress a.zip # Decompress multiple files ouch decompress a.zip b.tar.gz c.tar ``` The `-d/--dir` flag can be used to redirect decompression results to another directory. ```sh # Decompress 'summer_vacation.zip' inside of new folder 'pictures' ouch decompress summer_vacation.zip --dir pictures ``` ## Compressing Pass input files to the `compress` subcommand, add the **output file** at the end. ```sh # Compress two files into `archive.zip` ouch compress one.txt two.txt archive.zip # Compress file.txt using .lz4 and .zst ouch compress file.txt file.txt.lz4.zst ``` `ouch` detects the extensions of the **output file** to decide what formats to use. ## Listing ```sh ouch list archive.zip # Example with tree formatting ouch list source-code.zip --tree ``` Output: ``` └── src ├── archive │ ├── mod.rs │ ├── tar.rs │ └── zip.rs ├── utils │ ├── colors.rs │ ├── formatting.rs │ ├── mod.rs │ └── fs.rs ├── commands │ ├── list.rs │ ├── compress.rs │ ├── decompress.rs │ └── mod.rs ├── accessible.rs ├── error.rs ├── cli.rs └── main.rs ``` # Supported formats | Format | `.tar` | `.zip` | `.7z` | `.gz` | `.sz` | `.zst` | `.xz` | `.lzma` | `.lz` | `.bz`, `.bz2` | `.bz3` | `.lz4` | `.rar` | `.br` | |:---------:|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:| | Supported | ✓ | ✓¹ | ✓¹ | ✓² | ✓² | ✓² | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓³ | ✓ | ✓: Supports compression and decompression. ✓¹: Due to limitations of the compression format itself, (de)compression can't be done with streaming. ✓²: Supported, and compression runs in parallel. ✓³: Due to RAR's restrictive license, only decompression and listing can be supported. If you wish to exclude non-free code from your build, you can disable RAR support by building without the `unrar` feature. Aliases for these formats are also supported: - `tar`: `tgz`, `tbz`, `tbz2`, `tlz4`, `txz`, `tlzma`, `tsz`, `tzst`, `tlz`, `cbt` - `zip`: `cbz`, `epub` - `7z`: `cb7` - `rar`: `cbr` Formats can be chained: - `.tar.gz` - `.tar.gz.xz.zst.gz.lz4.sz` If the filename has no extensions, `ouch` will try to infer the format by the [file signature](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_file_signatures) and ask the user for confirmation. # Installation Refer to the packages list on the right. The most commonly used installation methods: ## On Arch Linux ```bash pacman -S ouch ``` ## On MacOS via Homebrew ```bash brew install ouch ``` ## On Windows via Scoop ```cmd scoop install ouch ``` ## From crates.io ```bash cargo install ouch ``` (If you're on Ubuntu, you might need to install `clang` to build it from crates.io.) ## Download the latest release bundle Check the [releases page](https://github.com/ouch-org/ouch/releases). Release binaries are signed with [Sigstore](https://sigstore.dev) via GitHub's artifact attestations. Verify a downloaded binary with the GitHub CLI: ``` gh attestation verify ouch-x86_64-unknown-linux-musl --repo ouch-org/ouch ``` ### Reproducing a release build Release builds are reproducible. Given the source at a tagged commit, anyone can rebuild the same binary and check that it matches what we shipped. Steps: ``` git clone https://github.com/ouch-org/ouch cd ouch git checkout export SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH=$(git log -1 --pretty=%ct) export RUSTFLAGS="--remap-path-prefix=$(pwd)=." cargo build --locked --release --target ``` The toolchain version is pinned in `rust-toolchain.toml` and rustup will install it automatically. Cross-compiled targets (anything using `cross-rs/cross`) inherit the cross Docker image's toolchain, which is not pinned by digest yet, so those targets are bit-for-bit reproducible only against the same `cross` image release. ## Compiling from source code Check the [wiki guide on compiling](https://github.com/ouch-org/ouch/wiki/Compiling-and-installing-from-source-code). # Benchmarks Benchmark results are available [here](benchmarks/results.md). Performance of compressing and decompressing [Rust](https://github.com/rust-lang/rust) source code is measured and compared with [Hyperfine](https://github.com/sharkdp/hyperfine). The values presented are the average (wall clock) elapsed time. Note: `ouch` focuses heavily on usage ergonomics and nice error messages, but we plan on doing some optimization in the future. Versions used: - `ouch` _0.4.0_ - [`tar`] _1.34_ - [`unzip`][infozip] _6.00_ - [`zip`][infozip] _3.0_ # Contributing Contributions of all sizes are welcome and appreciated! - Open an [issue](https://github.com/ouch-org/ouch/issues). - Package it for your favorite distribution or package manager. - Share it with a friend! - Open a pull request. If you're creating a Pull Request, check [CONTRIBUTING.md](./CONTRIBUTING.md). import os
import tarfile
import zipfile


def _tree(names):
    root = {}
    for raw in names:
        parts = [p for p in raw.split('/') if p]
        if not parts:
            continue
        node = root
        for part in parts:
            node = node.setdefault(part, {})
    out = []
    def walk(node, prefix=''):
        items = list(node.items())
        for i, (name, child) in enumerate(items):
            last = i == len(items)-1
            out.append(prefix + ('└── ' if last else '├── ') + name)
            walk(child, prefix + ('   ' if last else '│  '))
    walk(root)
    return out


def list_archive(path, tree=False):
    """Return archive listing lines including the Archive header."""
    label = os.fspath(path)

        with zipfile.ZipFile(path) as z:
            names = [i.filename for i in z.infolist()]

        with tarfile.open(path, 'r:*') as t:
            names = [m.name.rstrip('/') + ('/' if m.isdir() else '') for m in t.getmembers()]
    else:
        raise ValueError('unsupported archive format')
    body = _tree(names) if tree else names
    return [f'Archive: "{label}"'] + body

+    p = pathlib.PurePosixPath(name)
+    if p.is_absolute() or ".." in p.parts:
+        return None
+    target = os.path.abspath(os.path.join(root, *p.parts))
+    if os.path.commonpath((os.path.abspath(root), target)) != os.path.abspath(root):
+        return None
+    return target
+
+
+def _unpack_zip(zf, root):
+    count = 0
+    for info in zf.infolist():
+        target = _safe_target(root, info.filename)
+        if target is None:
+            continue
+        if info.is_dir():
+            os.makedirs(target, exist_ok=True)
+        else:
+            os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(target), exist_ok=True)
+            with zf.open(info) as src, open(target, "wb") as dst:
+                while True:
+                    block = src.read(1024 * 1024)
+                    if not block:
+                        break
+                    dst.write(block)
+        count += 1
+    return count
+
+
+def _unpack_tar(tf, root):
+    count = 0
+    for member in tf.getmembers():
+        target = _safe_target(root, member.name)
+        if target is None:
+            continue
+        if member.isdir():
+            os.makedirs(target, exist_ok=True)
+        elif member.isfile():
+            os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(target), exist_ok=True)
+            src = tf.extractfile(member)
+            if src:
+                with src, open(target, "wb") as dst:
+                    while True:
+                        block = src.read(1024 * 1024)
+                        if not block:
+                            break
+                        dst.write(block)
+                os.chmod(target, member.mode & 0o777)
+        elif member.issym() or member.islnk():
+            # Archive links can escape the output tree or affect later entries.
+            continue
+        else:
+            continue
+        count += 1
+    return count
+
+
+def decompress_file(path, output_dir=None, here=False, format=None):
+    """Extract a supported archive; return (destination, extracted-entry-count).
+
+    ZIP/TAR archives are extracted into a basename directory by default. A
+    single stream-compressed file is written beside the source under its
+    decompressed basename. `output_dir` overrides either destination.
+    """
+    path = os.fspath(path)
+    formats = formats_for(path, format)
+    if not formats:
+        raise ValueError("unsupported extension")
+    destination = "." if here else (os.fspath(output_dir) if output_dir else None)
+
+    if zipfile.is_zipfile(path):
+        if destination is None:
+            destination = output_name(path, formats)
+        os.makedirs(destination, exist_ok=True)
+        with zipfile.ZipFile(path) as zf:
+            return destination, _unpack_zip(zf, destination)
+
+    # Decode outer stream layers. This also recognizes chained TAR suffixes.
+    data = open(path, "rb").read()
+    remaining = formats[:]
+    while remaining and remaining[-1] in STREAMS:
+        fmt = remaining.pop()
+        if fmt == "gz":
+            data = gzip.decompress(data)
+        elif fmt in ("bz", "bz2"):
+            data = bz2.decompress(data)
+        else:
+            data = lzma.decompress(data)
+    if remaining and remaining[-1] == "tar":
+        if destination is None:
+            destination = output_name(path, formats)
+        os.makedirs(destination, exist_ok=True)
+        with tarfile.open(fileobj=io.BytesIO(data), mode="r:") as tf:
+            return destination, _unpack_tar(tf, destination)
+
+    if formats[-1] in STREAMS:
+        if destination is None:
+            destination = "." if here else (os.path.dirname(path) or ".")
+        os.makedirs(destination, exist_ok=True)
+        basename = output_name(path, formats)
+        target = os.path.join(destination, basename)
+        with open(target, "wb") as out:
+            out.write(data)
+        return destination, 1
+    raise ValueError("unsupported archive format")
*** End Patch";

#!/usr/bin/env python3
import os, sys, pathlib, shutil, gzip, bz2, lzma
from listing import list_archive
from compression import compress
from decompression import decompress_file, formats_for

VERSION = 'ouch 0.8.0'
EXTS = 'tar, zip, bz, bz2, bz3, gz, lz4, xz, lzma, lz, sz, zst, rar, 7z'
ALIASES = 'tgz, tbz, tlz4, txz, tlzma, tsz, tzst, tlz, cbt, cbz, epub, cb7, cbr'
ROOT_HELP = '''A command-line utility for easily compressing and decompressing files and directories.

Usage: executable [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>

Commands:
  compress    Compress one or more files into one output file [aliases: c]
  decompress  Decompresses one or more files, optionally into another folder [aliases: d]
  list        List contents of an archive [aliases: l, ls]
  help        Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

Options:
  -y, --yes                  Skip [Y/n] questions, default to yes
  -n, --no                   Skip [Y/n] questions, default to no
  -A, --accessible           Activate accessibility mode, reducing visual noise [env: ACCESSIBLE=]
  -H, --hidden               Ignore hidden files
  -q, --quiet                Silence output
  -g, --gitignore            Ignore files matched by git's ignore files
  -f, --format <FORMAT>      Specify the format of the archive
  -p, --password <PASSWORD>  Decompress or list with password
  -c, --threads <THREADS>    Concurrent working threads
  -h, --help                 Print help (see more with '--help')
  -V, --version              Print version
'''
COMMAND_HELP = {
'compress': '''Compress one or more files into one output file

Usage: executable compress [OPTIONS] <FILES>... <OUTPUT>

Arguments:
  <FILES>...  Files to be compressed
  <OUTPUT>    The resulting file. Its extensions can be used to specify the compression formats

Options:
  -l, --level <LEVEL>        Compression level, applied to all formats
  -y, --yes                  Skip [Y/n] questions, default to yes
      --fast                 Fastest compression level possible, conflicts with --level and --slow
  -n, --no                   Skip [Y/n] questions, default to no
  -A, --accessible           Activate accessibility mode, reducing visual noise [env: ACCESSIBLE=]
      --slow                 Slowest (and best) compression level possible, conflicts with --level and --fast
  -H, --hidden               Ignore hidden files
  -S, --follow-symlinks      Read from target files instead of from symlinks (relevant for `tar` and `zip`)
  -q, --quiet                Silence output
  -g, --gitignore            Ignore files matched by git's ignore files
  -f, --format <FORMAT>      Specify the format of the archive
  -p, --password <PASSWORD>  Decompress or list with password
  -c, --threads <THREADS>    Concurrent working threads
  -h, --help                 Print help
''',
'decompress': '''Decompresses one or more files, optionally into another folder

Usage: executable decompress [OPTIONS] <FILES>...

Arguments:
  <FILES>...  Files to be decompressed, or "-" for stdin

Options:
  -d, --dir <OUTPUT_DIR>     Decompress inside OUTPUT_DIR instead of the basename-derived subdirectory
  -y, --yes                  Skip [Y/n] questions, default to yes
      --here                 Extract directly into the current directory, like `tar -xf` and `unzip` do
  -n, --no                   Skip [Y/n] questions, default to no
  -A, --accessible           Activate accessibility mode, reducing visual noise [env: ACCESSIBLE=]
  -r, --remove               Remove the source file after successful decompression
  -H, --hidden               Ignore hidden files
  -q, --quiet                Silence output
  -g, --gitignore            Ignore files matched by git's ignore files
  -f, --format <FORMAT>      Specify the format of the archive
  -p, --password <PASSWORD>  Decompress or list with password
  -c, --threads <THREADS>    Concurrent working threads
  -h, --help                 Print help
''',
'list': '''List contents of an archive

Usage: executable list [OPTIONS] <ARCHIVES>...

Arguments:
  <ARCHIVES>...  Archives whose contents should be listed

Options:
  -t, --tree                 Show archive contents as a tree
  -y, --yes                  Skip [Y/n] questions, default to yes
  -n, --no                   Skip [Y/n] questions, default to no
  -A, --accessible           Activate accessibility mode, reducing visual noise [env: ACCESSIBLE=]
  -H, --hidden               Ignore hidden files
  -q, --quiet                Silence output
  -g, --gitignore            Ignore files matched by git's ignore files
  -f, --format <FORMAT>      Specify the format of the archive
  -p, --password <PASSWORD>  Decompress or list with password
  -c, --threads <THREADS>    Concurrent working threads
  -h, --help                 Print help
'''}

def die(msg, code=1):
    print(msg, file=sys.stderr); raise SystemExit(code)

def parse(argv, command):
    opts={'yes':False,'no':False,'quiet':False,'format':None,'tree':False,'here':False,'dir':None,'remove':False,'level':None,'fast':False,'slow':False,'follow':False}
    pos=[]; i=0
    takes={'-f':'format','--format':'format','-p':'password','--password':'password','-c':'threads','--threads':'threads','-l':'level','--level':'level','-d':'dir','--dir':'dir'}
    flags={'-y':'yes','--yes':'yes','-n':'no','--no':'no','-q':'quiet','--quiet':'quiet','-t':'tree','--tree':'tree','--here':'here','-r':'remove','--remove':'remove','--fast':'fast','--slow':'slow','-S':'follow','--follow-symlinks':'follow'}
    while i<len(argv):
        a=argv[i]
        if a in ('-h','--help'): print(COMMAND_HELP[command],end=''); raise SystemExit(0)
        if a in ('-A','--accessible','-H','--hidden','-g','--gitignore'): i+=1; continue
        if a in flags: opts[flags[a]]=True
        elif a.startswith('--') and '=' in a and a.split('=',1)[0] in takes:
            k,v=a.split('=',1); opts[takes[k]]=v
        elif a in takes:
            i+=1
            if i>=len(argv): die(f"error: a value is required for '{a}'\n\nFor more information, try '--help'.",2)
            opts[takes[a]]=argv[i]
        elif a.startswith('-') and a!='-': die(f"error: unexpected argument '{a}' found\n\nFor more information, try '--help'.",2)
        else: pos.append(a)
        i+=1
    if opts['fast'] and opts['slow']: die("error: the argument '--fast' cannot be used with '--slow'\n\nUsage: executable compress --fast <FILES>... <OUTPUT>\n\nFor more information, try '--help'.",2)
    if opts['fast'] and opts['level'] is not None or opts['slow'] and opts['level'] is not None: die("error: the argument '--level <LEVEL>' cannot be used with '--fast'\n\nFor more information, try '--help'.",2)
    if opts['here'] and opts['dir']: die("error: the argument '--here' cannot be used with '--dir <OUTPUT_DIR>'\n\nFor more information, try '--help'.",2)
    if opts['level'] is not None:
        try: opts['level']=int(opts['level'])
        except: die(f"error: invalid value '{opts['level']}' for '--level <LEVEL>': invalid digit found in string\n\nFor more information, try '--help'.",2)
    return opts,pos

def missing(path):
    die(f"[ERROR] failed to canonicalize path `{path}`: No such file or directory (os error 2)\n - File not found")

def ext_formats(path, override=None):
    if override: return [x.lower() for x in override.split('.') if x]
    parts=pathlib.Path(path).name.split('.')
    return [x.lower() for x in parts[1:] if x]

def main(argv):
    if not argv or argv[0] in ('-h','--help'): print(ROOT_HELP,end=''); return 0
    if argv[0] in ('-V','--version'): print(VERSION); return 0
    if argv[0]=='help':
        cmd=argv[1] if len(argv)>1 else None
        if cmd in ('c',): cmd='compress'
        if cmd in ('d',): cmd='decompress'
        if cmd in ('l','ls'): cmd='list'
        print(COMMAND_HELP.get(cmd,ROOT_HELP),end=''); return 0
    cmd=argv.pop(0); cmd={'c':'compress','d':'decompress','l':'list','ls':'list'}.get(cmd,cmd)
    if cmd not in COMMAND_HELP: die(f"error: unrecognized subcommand '{cmd}'\n\nUsage: executable [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>\n\nFor more information, try '--help'.",2)
    opts,pos=parse(argv,cmd)
    required={'compress':2,'decompress':1,'list':1}[cmd]
    if len(pos)<required:
        args={'compress':'  <FILES>...\n  <OUTPUT>','decompress':'  <FILES>...','list':'  <ARCHIVES>...'}[cmd]
        if cmd=='compress' and len(pos)==1: args='  <FILES>...'
        die(f"error: the following required arguments were not provided:\n{args}\n\nUsage: executable {cmd} {'<FILES>... <OUTPUT>' if cmd=='compress' else '<FILES>...' if cmd=='decompress' else '<ARCHIVES>...'}\n\nFor more information, try '--help'.",2)
    if cmd=='compress':
        inputs=pos[:-1]; output=pos[-1]
        for p in inputs:
            if not os.path.exists(p): missing(p)
        fmts=ext_formats(output,opts['format'])
        if not fmts:
            die(f'[ERROR] Cannot compress to "{output}"\n - You must supply the compression format\n\nhint: Try adding supported extensions (see --help):\nhint:   ouch compress <FILES>... {output}.tar.gz\nhint:   ouch compress <FILES>... {output}.zip\nhint: \nhint: Alternatively, you can overwrite this option by using the \'--format\' flag:\nhint:   ouch compress <FILES>... {output} --format tar.gz')
        try: compress(inputs,output,fmts,opts['level'],opts['follow'])
        except Exception as e: die(f'[ERROR] {e}')
        if not opts['quiet']:
            print(f'[INFO] Compressing "{inputs[0]}"')
            try: print(f'[INFO] Output file size: {os.path.getsize(output):.2f}   B')
            except: pass
            print(f'[INFO] Successfully compressed to "{output}"')
        return 0
    if cmd=='list':
        for path in pos:
            if not os.path.exists(path): missing(path)
            try:
                lines=list_archive(path,opts['tree'])
                if opts['quiet']: lines=lines[1:]
                for line in lines: print(line)
            except Exception:
                die(f'[ERROR] Cannot list archive contents\n - Only archives can have their contents listed\n - Files are not archives: "{path}"')
        return 0
    for path in pos:
        if path!='-' and not os.path.exists(path): missing(path)
        fmts=ext_formats(path,opts['format'])
        if not fmts:
            die(f'[ERROR] Cannot decompress files\n - Files with missing extensions: "{path}"\n - Decompression formats are detected automatically from file extension and signature\n\nhint: Supported extensions are: {EXTS}\nhint: Supported aliases are: {ALIASES}\nhint: \nhint: Alternatively, you can pass an extension to the \'--format\' flag:\nhint:   ouch decompress {path} --format tar.gz')
        try:
            dest,count=decompress_file(path,opts['dir'],opts['here'],opts['format'])
            if opts['remove'] and path!='-': os.remove(path)
            if not opts['quiet']:
                if path=='-': print('[INFO] STDIN decompressed to "ouch-output"')
                else: print(f'[INFO] Decompressed "{path}" to "{dest}"')
                print(f'[INFO] Decompressed {count} files')
        except Exception as e: die(f'[ERROR] Cannot decompress files\n - {e}')
    return 0

if __name__=='__main__':
    try: raise SystemExit(main(sys.argv[1:]))
    except BrokenPipeError: raise SystemExit(1)

"""Standard-library extraction helpers for ouch-style archives."""
import bz2
import gzip
import io
import lzma
import os
import pathlib
import sys
import tarfile
import zipfile


ALIASES = {
    "tgz": ["tar", "gz"], "tbz": ["tar", "bz2"], "tbz2": ["tar", "bz2"],
    "txz": ["tar", "xz"], "tlzma": ["tar", "lzma"], "tzst": ["tar", "zst"],
    "tlz": ["tar", "lz"], "tlz4": ["tar", "lz4"], "tsz": ["tar", "sz"],
    "cbz": ["zip"], "epub": ["zip"], "cb7": ["7z"], "cbr": ["rar"],
}
STREAMS = {"gz", "bz", "bz2", "xz", "lzma"}


def formats_for(path, override=None):
    if override:
        values = [x.lstrip(".") for x in override.split(".") if x]
    else:
        values = pathlib.Path(os.fspath(path)).name.split(".")[1:]
    if len(values) == 1 and values[0] in ALIASES:
        values = ALIASES[values[0]][:]
    return values


def output_name(path, formats=None):
    if os.fspath(path) == "-":
        return "ouch-output"
    name = os.path.basename(os.fspath(path))
    values = formats if formats is not None else formats_for(path)
    parts = name.split(".")
    raw_suffix = parts[-1].lower() if len(parts) > 1 else ""
    strip_count = 1 if raw_suffix in ALIASES else len(values)
    if strip_count and len(parts) > strip_count:
        name = ".".join(parts[:-strip_count])
    if not name:
        name = "ouch-output"
    return name


def _safe_target(root, name):
    # Reject absolute paths and traversal, including Windows separators.
    name = name.replace("\\", "/")
    p = pathlib.PurePosixPath(name)
    if p.is_absolute() or ".." in p.parts:
        return None
    target = os.path.abspath(os.path.join(root, *p.parts))
    if os.path.commonpath((os.path.abspath(root), target)) != os.path.abspath(root):
        return None
    return target


def _safe_link(root, link_path, link_name):
    """Return a relative link target only when its resolution stays in root."""
    link_name = link_name.replace("\\", "/")
    if link_name.startswith("/"):
        return None
    parent = os.path.dirname(link_path)
    resolved = os.path.abspath(os.path.join(parent, link_name))

## Task and constraints

Recreate `/opt/reference/executable` (`ouch` 0.8.0) in Python 3.10 using only the bundled docs and reference behavior. Do not use external source code or delegate to the reference at runtime. Implementation is in `/workspace`; `compile.sh` is provided and must not be run. User explicitly wants continued work and tool use: review the latest shared `main`, compare against the reference, fix mismatches, and push.

## Current progress

The shared `team/main` has a working CLI plus modules for compression, listing, and decompression. I have contributed and pushed:

- `decompression.py`: safe ZIP/TAR extraction, symlinks, stdin support, recognized suffix parsing, aliases including `cbt`, and ZIP wrapped in gzip/bz2/xz support.
- `listing.py`: automatic listing of ZIP archives wrapped in supported stream encodings.
- Fixed a `main.py` indentation regression that caused a SyntaxError; subsequently brisk_harbor also fixed a shared syntax regression.
- Posted findings and coordinated with teammates through `group`.

Manual comparisons so far covered root and subcommand help, ZIP/TAR/gzip operations, nested ZIP tree formatting, ZIP.gz listing/compression/extraction, stdin gzip extraction, symlink extraction, case-sensitive suffix fallback, and malformed archive diagnostics. `python3 -m py_compile` passed after the syntax fix.

## Current state

At the start of the latest turn, I fetched and fast-forwarded to `team/main` at `32ee9ad` (merge commit), including `4b412f1 Match empty archive notice path formatting`. No local changes were reported. Latest group feed includes brisk_harbor’s syntax regression fix and a TAR smoke-test match.

The current active instruction is to keep reviewing and testing; do not stop after a progress report.

## Next steps

1. Inspect latest `main.py`, `listing.py`, `compression.py`, and `decompression.py` for likely gaps.
2. Pick unexplored reference cases, compare behavior, and make concrete fixes. Useful areas: global/command option edge cases, malformed archives, compressed aliases/chains, overwrite behavior, extraction path handling.
3. Run the implementation with `python3 main.py ...` (do not run `compile.sh`).
4. Before pushing, fetch `team/main`, merge/fast-forward, then push `HEAD:main`; coordinate in `group` if touching a teammate’s active module.
5. Keep the user updated with concise commentary during tool work and finish with a self-contained status.
I’ll review the latest shared CLI and the open listing/extraction findings, then probe the reference for a case that can improve coverage and push any fix.

def help_text(name):
    resource = {'root':'help_long.txt', 'short':'help_short.txt', 'compress':'help_compress.txt',
                'decompress':'help_decompress.txt', 'list':'help_list.txt'}[name]
    path = pathlib.Path(__file__).resolve().parent / 'test_assets' / 'test_resources' / resource
    return path.read_text().replace('Usage: ouch ', 'Usage: executable ')

def die(msg, code=1):
    if ACCESSIBLE: msg=msg.replace('[ERROR] ', 'ERROR: ')
    print(msg, file=sys.stderr); raise SystemExit(code)

def parse(argv, command):
    opts={'yes':False,'no':False,'quiet':False,'format':None,'tree':False,'here':False,'dir':None,'remove':False,'level':None,'fast':False,'slow':False,'follow':False,'hidden':False,'gitignore':False}
    pos=[]; i=0
    takes={'-f':'format','--format':'format','-p':'password','--password':'password','-c':'threads','--threads':'threads','-l':'level','--level':'level','-d':'dir','--dir':'dir'}
    flags={'-y':'yes','--yes':'yes','-n':'no','--no':'no','-q':'quiet','--quiet':'quiet','-t':'tree','--tree':'tree','--here':'here','-r':'remove','--remove':'remove','--fast':'fast','--slow':'slow','-S':'follow','--follow-symlinks':'follow'}
    short_flags={'y','n','q','t','r','S','A','H','g'}
    normalized=[]
    for token in argv:
        if token.startswith('-') and not token.startswith('--') and len(token)>2 and all(ch in short_flags for ch in token[1:]):
            normalized.extend('-'+ch for ch in token[1:])
        else:
            normalized.append(token)
    argv=normalized
    while i<len(argv):
        a=argv[i]
        if a in ('-h','--help'): print(help_text(command),end=''); raise SystemExit(0)
        if a in ('-A','--accessible'):
            global ACCESSIBLE
            ACCESSIBLE=True
            i+=1; continue
        if a in ('-H','--hidden'): opts['hidden']=True; i+=1; continue
        if a in ('-g','--gitignore'): opts['gitignore']=True; i+=1; continue
        if a in flags: opts[flags[a]]=True
        elif a.startswith('--') and '=' in a and a.split('=',1)[0] in takes:
            k,v=a.split('=',1); opts[takes[k]]=v
        elif a in takes:
            i+=1
            if i>=len(argv): die(f"error: a value is required for '{a}'\n\nFor more information, try '--help'.",2)
            if takes[a]=='threads' and argv[i].startswith('-'):
                value=argv[i]
                usage={'compress':'Usage: executable compress [OPTIONS] <FILES>... <OUTPUT>','decompress':'Usage: executable decompress [OPTIONS] <FILES>...','list':'Usage: executable list [OPTIONS] <ARCHIVES>...'}[command]
                die(f"error: unexpected argument '{value}' found\n\n  tip: to pass '{value}' as a value, use '-- {value}'\n\n{usage}\n\nFor more information, try '--help'.",2)
            opts[takes[a]]=argv[i]
        elif a.startswith('-') and a!='-':
            usage={'compress':'Usage: executable compress [OPTIONS] <FILES>... <OUTPUT>','decompress':'Usage: executable decompress [OPTIONS] <FILES>...','list':'Usage: executable list [OPTIONS] <ARCHIVES>...'}[command]
            tip=f"\n\n  tip: to pass '{a}' as a value, use '-- --{a.lstrip('-')}'" if a.startswith('--') else ''
            die(f"error: unexpected argument '{a}' found{tip}\n\n{usage}\n\nFor more information, try '--help'.",2)
        else: pos.append(a)
        i+=1
    if opts['fast'] and opts['slow']: die("error: the argument '--fast' cannot be used with '--slow'\n\nUsage: executable compress --fast <FILES>... <OUTPUT>\n\nFor more information, try '--help'.",2)
    if opts['yes'] and opts['no']:
        tail='<FILES>... <OUTPUT>' if command=='compress' else '<FILES>...' if command=='decompress' else '<ARCHIVES>...'
        die(f"error: the argument '--yes' cannot be used with '--no'\n\nUsage: executable {command} --yes {tail}\n\nFor more information, try '--help'.",2)
    if opts['fast'] and opts['level'] is not None: die("error: the argument '--fast' cannot be used with '--level <LEVEL>'\n\nUsage: executable compress --fast <FILES>... <OUTPUT>\n\nFor more information, try '--help'.",2)
    if opts['slow'] and opts['level'] is not None: die("error: the argument '--slow' cannot be used with '--level <LEVEL>'\n\nUsage: executable compress --slow <FILES>... <OUTPUT>\n\nFor more information, try '--help'.",2)
    if opts['here'] and opts['dir']: die("error: the argument '--here' cannot be used with '--dir <OUTPUT_DIR>'\n\nUsage: executable decompress --here <FILES>...\n\nFor more information, try '--help'.",2)
    if opts['level'] is not None:
        try: opts['level']=int(opts['level'])
        except: die(f"error: invalid value '{opts['level']}' for '--level <LEVEL>': invalid digit found in string\n\nFor more information, try '--help'.",2)
    if opts.get('threads') is not None:
        try: opts['threads']=int(opts['threads'])
        except: die(f"error: invalid value '{opts['threads']}' for '--threads <THREADS>': invalid digit found in string\n\nFor more information, try '--help'.",2)
        if opts['threads'] < 0: die(f"error: invalid value '{opts['threads']}' for '--threads <THREADS>': invalid digit found in string\n\nFor more information, try '--help'.",2)
    return opts,pos

def missing(path):
    die(f"[ERROR] failed to canonicalize path `{path}`: No such file or directory (os error 2)\n - File not found")

def resolve_output_conflict(path, opts):
    if not os.path.exists(path): return path
    if opts['yes']: return path
    if opts['no']: return None
    while True:
        prompt=f'Handle file conflict for "{path}": [(R)ename/(o)verwrite/(s)kip]'
        print(prompt, flush=True)
        try: answer=input().strip().lower()
        except EOFError:
            die(f'[ERROR] Unexpected EOF when asking question\n - When asking the user:\n -   "Handle file conflict for "{path}:"\n - Expected one of the options as answer, but found EOF instead.\n\nhint: If using Ouch in scripting, consider using `--yes` and `--no`.')
        if answer in ('o','overwrite'): return path
        if answer in ('s','skip'): return None
        if answer in ('r','rename'):
            folder=os.path.dirname(path)
            name=os.path.basename(path)
            stem,ext=os.path.splitext(name)
            index=1
            while True:
                candidate=os.path.join(folder, f'{stem}_{index}{ext}')
                if not os.path.exists(candidate): return candidate
                index+=1

def display_path(path):
    try:
        absolute=os.path.abspath(os.fspath(path))
        cwd=os.path.abspath(os.getcwd())
        if os.path.commonpath((cwd,absolute))==cwd:
            return os.path.relpath(absolute,cwd)
        return absolute
    except Exception: return os.fspath(path)

def display_decompressed(path):
    # Ouch echoes explicitly supplied absolute extraction roots verbatim.
    return os.fspath(path) if os.path.isabs(os.fspath(path)) else display_path(path)

def size_text(size):
    if size < 1000: return f'{size:6.2f}   B'
    if size < 1000**2: return f'{size/1000:6.2f} kiB'
    if size < 1000**3: return f'{size/1000**2:6.2f} MiB'
    return f'{size/1000**3:6.2f} GiB'

def warn_zip_stream(formats):
    if 'zip' in formats and any(fmt in ('gz','bz','bz2','xz','lzma') for fmt in formats[formats.index('zip')+1:]):
        print("[WARNING]: \n  The format '.zip' is limited by design and cannot be (de)compressed with encoding streams.\n  When chaining '.zip' with other formats, all (de)compression needs to be done in-memory\n  Careful, you might run out of RAM if the archive is too large!")

def extracted_entries(archive_path, destination):
    entries=[]
    try:
        formats=formats_for(archive_path)
        data=open(archive_path,'rb').read()
        for fmt in reversed(formats):
            if fmt=='gz': data=gzip.decompress(data)
            elif fmt in ('bz','bz2'): data=bz2.decompress(data)
            elif fmt in ('xz','lzma'): data=lzma.decompress(data)
            else: break
        if formats and formats[0]=='zip':
            with zipfile.ZipFile(io.BytesIO(data)) as archive:
                entries=[(i.filename, i.file_size) for i in archive.infolist() if not i.is_dir()]
        elif formats and formats[0]=='tar':
            with tarfile.open(fileobj=io.BytesIO(data),mode='r:') as archive:
                entries=[(i.name, i.size) for i in archive.getmembers() if not i.isdir()]
    except Exception:
        return []
    result=[]
    for name,size in entries:
        path=os.path.join(destination,name)
        if os.path.lexists(path): result.append((path,size))
    return result

def ext_formats(path, override=None):
    if override: return [x for x in override.split('.') if x]
    parts=pathlib.Path(path).name.split('.')
    known=set(EXTS.split(', ')) | set(ALIASES.split(', '))
    values=[]
    for suffix in reversed(parts[1:]):
        if suffix not in known: break
        values.append(suffix)
    return list(reversed(values))

SUPPORTED=set(EXTS.split(', '))
FORMAT_ALIASES={'tgz':['tar','gz'],'tbz':['tar','bz2'],'tbz2':['tar','bz2'],'tlz4':['tar','lz4'],'txz':['tar','xz'],'tlzma':['tar','lzma'],'tsz':['tar','sz'],'tzst':['tar','zst'],'tlz':['tar','lz'],'cbt':['tar'],'cbz':['zip'],'epub':['zip'],'cb7':['7z'],'cbr':['rar']}

def invalid_format(formats):
    expanded=FORMAT_ALIASES.get(formats[0],formats) if len(formats)==1 else formats
    return next((x for x in expanded if x not in SUPPORTED),None)

def format_parse_error(value):
    bad=invalid_format([x for x in value.split('.') if x]) or value
    die(f"[ERROR] Failed to parse `--format {value}`\n - Unsupported extension '{bad}'\n\nhint: Supported extensions are: {EXTS}\nhint: Supported aliases are: {ALIASES}\nhint: \nhint: Examples:\nhint:   --format tar\nhint:   --format gz\nhint:   --format tar.gz")

# Ouch! `ouch` stands for **Obvious Unified Compression Helper**. It's a CLI tool for compressing and decompressing various formats. - [Features](#features) - [Usage](#usage) - [Installation](#installation) - [Supported Formats](#supported-formats) - [Benchmarks](#benchmarks) - [Contributing](#contributing) # Features 1. Easy to use. 2. Fast. 3. Great error message feedback. 4. No runtime dependencies. 5. Accessibility mode ([see more](https://github.com/ouch-org/ouch/wiki/Accessibility)). 6. Shell completions and man pages. # Usage `ouch` has three main subcommands: - `ouch decompress` (alias `d`) - `ouch compress` (alias `c`) - `ouch list` (alias `l` or `ls`) To see `help` for a specific command: ```sh ouch help ouch --help # equivalent ``` ## Decompressing Use the `decompress` subcommand, `ouch` will detect the extensions automatically. ```sh ouch decompress a.zip # Decompress multiple files ouch decompress a.zip b.tar.gz c.tar ``` The `-d/--dir` flag can be used to redirect decompression results to another directory. ```sh # Decompress 'summer_vacation.zip' inside of new folder 'pictures' ouch decompress summer_vacation.zip --dir pictures ``` ## Compressing Pass input files to the `compress` subcommand, add the **output file** at the end. ```sh # Compress two files into `archive.zip` ouch compress one.txt two.txt archive.zip # Compress file.txt using .lz4 and .zst ouch compress file.txt file.txt.lz4.zst ``` `ouch` detects the extensions of the **output file** to decide what formats to use. ## Listing ```sh ouch list archive.zip # Example with tree formatting ouch list source-code.zip --tree ``` Output: ``` └── src ├── archive │ ├── mod.rs │ ├── tar.rs │ └── zip.rs ├── utils │ ├── colors.rs │ ├── formatting.rs │ ├── mod.rs │ └── fs.rs ├── commands │ ├── list.rs │ ├── compress.rs │ ├── decompress.rs │ └── mod.rs ├── accessible.rs ├── error.rs ├── cli.rs └── main.rs ``` # Supported formats | Format | `.tar` | `.zip` | `.7z` | `.gz` | `.sz` | `.zst` | `.xz` | `.lzma` | `.lz` | `.bz`, `.bz2` | `.bz3` | `.lz4` | `.rar` | `.br` | |:---------:|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:| | Supported | ✓ | ✓¹ | ✓¹ | ✓² | ✓² | ✓² | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓³ | ✓ | ✓: Supports compression and decompression. ✓¹: Due to limitations of the compression format itself, (de)compression can't be done with streaming. ✓²: Supported, and compression runs in parallel. ✓³: Due to RAR's restrictive license, only decompression and listing can be supported. If you wish to exclude non-free code from your build, you can disable RAR support by building without the `unrar` feature. Aliases for these formats are also supported: - `tar`: `tgz`, `tbz`, `tbz2`, `tlz4`, `txz`, `tlzma`, `tsz`, `tzst`, `tlz`, `cbt` - `zip`: `cbz`, `epub` - `7z`: `cb7` - `rar`: `cbr` Formats can be chained: - `.tar.gz` - `.tar.gz.xz.zst.gz.lz4.sz` If the filename has no extensions, `ouch` will try to infer the format by the [file signature](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_file_signatures) and ask the user for confirmation. # Installation Refer to the packages list on the right. The most commonly used installation methods: ## On Arch Linux ```bash pacman -S ouch ``` ## On MacOS via Homebrew ```bash brew install ouch ``` ## On Windows via Scoop ```cmd scoop install ouch ``` ## From crates.io ```bash cargo install ouch ``` (If you're on Ubuntu, you might need to install `clang` to build it from crates.io.) ## Download the latest release bundle Check the [releases page](https://github.com/ouch-org/ouch/releases). """ZIP/TAR output helpers for ouch-compatible compression."""
import bz2
import gzip
import fnmatch
import lzma
import os
import stat
import struct
import zlib
import tarfile
import zipfile


def _members(paths, follow_symlinks=False, ignore_hidden=False, use_gitignore=False):
    """Yield archive members in the host filesystem's depth-first order."""
    def read_patterns(directory, base):
        rules=[]
        if not use_gitignore: return rules
        try:
            with open(os.path.join(directory,'.gitignore'),encoding='utf-8',errors='replace') as f:
                for raw in f:
                    pat=raw.strip()
                    if not pat or pat.startswith('#'): continue
                    neg=pat.startswith('!')
                    if neg: pat=pat[1:]
                    prefix=os.path.relpath(directory,base).replace(os.sep,'/')
                    if prefix=='.': prefix=''
                    rules.append((prefix,pat,neg))
        except OSError: pass
        return rules

    def ignored(rel, is_dir, rules):
        rel=rel.replace(os.sep,'/')
        skip=False
        for prefix,pat,neg in rules:
            if pat.startswith('\\#') or pat.startswith('\\!'): pat=pat[1:]
            target=rel[len(prefix)+1:] if prefix and rel.startswith(prefix+'/') else ('' if rel==prefix else rel)
            if prefix and not (rel==prefix or rel.startswith(prefix+'/')): continue
            directory_only=pat.endswith('/')
            pat=pat.strip('/')
            anchored='/' in pat
            parts=target.split('/')
            matched=fnmatch.fnmatchcase(target,pat) if anchored else any(fnmatch.fnmatchcase(part,pat) for part in parts)
            if directory_only and not is_dir and not matched:
                matched=any(fnmatch.fnmatchcase('/'.join(parts[:i]),pat) for i in range(1,len(parts)))
            if matched: skip=not neg
        return skip

    def descend(directory, base, rules):
        rules=rules+read_patterns(directory,base)
        try:
            entries = list(os.scandir(directory))
        except OSError:
            return
        for entry in entries:
            if ignore_hidden and entry.name.startswith('.'):
                continue
            full = entry.path
            rel=os.path.relpath(full,base)
            is_dir=entry.is_dir(follow_symlinks=follow_symlinks)
            if use_gitignore and ignored(rel,is_dir,rules): continue
            yield full, rel
            if is_dir:
                yield from descend(full, base, rules)

    for src in paths:
        src = os.fspath(src)
        name = os.path.basename(os.path.normpath(src)) or src
        if os.path.islink(src) and not follow_symlinks:
            yield src, name
            if os.path.isdir(src):
                base = os.path.dirname(os.path.normpath(src)) or "."
                yield from descend(src, base, read_patterns(base, base))
        elif os.path.isdir(src):
            yield src, name
            base = os.path.dirname(os.path.normpath(src)) or "."
            yield from descend(src, base, read_patterns(base, base))
        else:
            yield src, name


def compress(inputs, output, formats=None, level=None, follow_symlinks=False, ignore_hidden=False, use_gitignore=False):
    """Create ZIP/TAR and optional stream layers. Returns output path.

    ``formats`` are ordered inner-to-outer, e.g. ["tar", "gz"].
    """
    formats = [str(x).lower().lstrip(".") for x in (formats or [])]
    aliases = {"tgz": ["tar", "gz"], "tbz": ["tar", "bz2"],
               "tbz2": ["tar", "bz2"], "txz": ["tar", "xz"],
               "tlzma": ["tar", "lzma"], "tzst": ["tar", "zst"],
               "tlz": ["tar", "lz"], "tlz4": ["tar", "lz4"],
               "tsz": ["tar", "sz"], "cbt": ["tar"], "cbz": ["zip"], "epub": ["zip"],
               "cb7": ["7z"]}
    if len(formats) == 1 and formats[0] in aliases:
